headline: Record sales, orders and profit; full-year guidance raised
summary_short: Teledyne's Q2 2026 net sales rose 9.8% y/y to $1,662.5M with GAAP operating margin at 20.0% (up from 18.4%) and net income up 19.9% to $251.7M ($5.37 diluted EPS); the company raised its full-year 2026 GAAP EPS outlook to $20.73-$20.99 from $20.08-$20.44.
summary_long: Sales grew across all four segments, led by Digital Imaging (+12.7% y/y) on higher infrared/detector demand for defense and commercial applications; management cited record quarterly orders, sales and operating profit, with GAAP operating margin expanding to 20.0% from 18.4% and non-GAAP margin to 23.4% from 22.2%. Net income rose 19.9% to $251.7M ($5.37 diluted EPS); non-GAAP diluted EPS was $6.28, +20.8% y/y. Teledyne repaid a $450M debt maturity in the quarter, cutting net debt to $1,686.9M from $2,123.0M at year-end, while cash fell to $340.1M. The company raised full-year 2026 GAAP EPS guidance to $20.73-$20.99 (from $20.08-$20.44) and non-GAAP EPS to $24.45-$24.65 (from $23.85-$24.15), and issued Q3 2026 GAAP EPS guidance of $5.10-$5.25.

drivers.explanation: Growth was led by Digital Imaging's higher infrared detector, surveillance and X-ray sales for defense and commercial customers, plus gains in every product line within Instrumentation and across Aerospace and Defense Electronics and Engineered Systems.

Digital Imaging profit surged on higher sales, favorable product mix and tariff refunds, partly offset by higher R&D and inventory reserves; Instrumentation profit was flat to down on unfavorable mix.
Tracked higher operating income and lower net interest expense after debt repayment, partly offset by a higher 21.7% effective tax rate versus 19.3% a year earlier.
EPS growth outpaced net income growth (+19.9%) because weighted diluted shares fell slightly to 46.9 million from 47.4 million a year earlier.
Cash declined as the company used $450 million to repay a debt maturity in the quarter, more than offsetting $315.2 million of operating cash flow.
Debt fell after Teledyne repaid a $450 million fixed-rate note during the quarter, lowering net debt to $1,686.9 million from $2,123.0 million at year-end.

Management cited the strongest quarterly orders, sales and operating profit in company history, with organic growth strongest in Digital Imaging's infrared and unmanned-systems products; raised FY2026 EPS guidance and continues reviewing acquisitions given balance-sheet strength.
